channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Optimising exercise prescription for cancer-related fatigue, lean mass, physical function and muscle strength in women with breast cancer: a systematic review with dose-response network meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and dose-response network meta-analysis (64 trials, n=5156) found that combined exercise was most effective for improving cancer-related fatigue and lean mass, while resistance exercise was most effective for physical function and muscle strength in women with breast cancer, with significant benefits achievable at doses as low as 10–40 min/week.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Effects of supervised exercise during pregnancy on gestational diabetes mellitus and other pregnancy outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis (19 studies, n=6213) found that supervised exercise during pregnancy significantly reduced the risk of gestational diabetes (RR 0.74), gestational hypertension (RR 0.55), excessive gestational weight gain (RR 0.75), and macrosomia (RR 0.61), with greater effects from earlier intervention, higher adherence, combined aerobic and resistance training, and ≥150 min/week exercise.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Physical Exercise Reduces Fall-Related Outcomes Among People With Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (1536 participants) found that physical exercise significantly reduced the number of falls by 39% (IRR = 0.61, 95% CI = [0.47, 0.78]) among people with stroke. Balance training and programs integrating cognitive components were most effective, particularly for those in the chronic stage with mild to moderate disability.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of TENS, NMES, and Combination Therapy on Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain and Function After Stroke.
item.description: This prospective randomized study (n=60) found that combined TENS and NMES significantly reduced hemiplegic shoulder pain and improved SPADI scores more than TENS alone, and also improved shoulder ROM, in acute and subacute stroke patients, when added to a standardized rehabilitation program.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Short-Term Effects of Radial Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy in Addition to Physiotherapy on Spasticity, Walking Performance, and Quality of Life in Chronic Stroke: A Sham-Controlled Randomized Trial.
item.description: This sham-controlled RCT (n=85) found that adding 4 weeks of radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy to physiotherapy significantly improved spasticity (-0.56 MAS points), walking performance (-1.41s 10MWT), functional mobility, motor function, and quality of life in chronic stroke patients with plantar flexor spasticity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Video-based education is non-inferior to in-person education in patients undergoing arthroscopic partial meniscectomy: a non-inferiority randomized controlled trial | Archives of Physiotherapy
item.description: A non-inferiority RCT (n=166) found that preoperative video-based education was non-inferior to postoperative in-person education for pain-related self-efficacy (PSEQ MD: -0.6 at T1; -0.5 at T2) and led to better fear of movement scores (TSK) in patients undergoing arthroscopic partial meniscectomy.
item.author: Arch Physiother

item.title: Physical Therapy Management of Fall Risk in Community-Dwelling Older Adults (CPG+)
item.description: APTA Geriatrics has published an updated Clinical Practice Guideline (CPG+) for the physical therapy management of fall risk in community-dwelling adults aged 65 and over, replacing the 2015 version and including a clinical reasoning algorithm.
item.author: APTA

item.title: The effect of multimodal sensory therapy in consciousness improvement in patients with acquired brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis (18 studies, 884 participants) found that multimodal sensory therapy significantly improved consciousness levels (SMD, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.04-1.92) and increased the odds of coma emergence (OR, 9.85; 95% CI, 3.86-25.01) in adults with acquired brain injury-related disorders of consciousness.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise-only interventions and exercise-based multidomain lifestyle interventions to promote cognitive function in older adults without dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 227 studies found that exercise-only interventions significantly improved executive functions, memory, and processing speed in older adults without dementia compared to control. Exercise-plus interventions (exercise combined with other lifestyle factors) were significantly better than control for memory, and better than exercise-only for executive functions and processing speed, but not memory.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Effects of Exergames on Fundamental Movement Skills in Childhood: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 studies (17 comparisons) concluded that low-barrier exergames are as effective as traditional activities for fundamental movement skill adaptation in children. The variability in effects was explained by coaching and activity structure, rather than exergame status itself.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Fatigue-related neuromuscular outcomes following ACL reconstruction: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 studies (n=477) found that individuals with ACLR demonstrated lower post-fatigue quadriceps CAR (SMD: -0.69, p < 0.001) and muscle activation patterns (SMD: -0.62, p < 0.001) compared to healthy controls, with moderate certainty of evidence.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Motor-Based Interventions in Children with Developmental Coordination Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials - Sports Medicine - Open
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 32 RCTs found that motor-based interventions (MBI) significantly improved overall motor skills (g=1.00), balance (g=0.57), cognitive (g=1.53), and activity performance (g=0.71) in children with DCD. Task-oriented training showed particular effectiveness, but MBI did not significantly improve psychosocial factors or participation levels.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Approach to sarcopenia in older adults: a systematic review of dietary and exercise interventions in the primary care setting
item.description: A systematic review of 6 studies (n=444 in experimental groups) on sarcopenia in older adults found that combined physical exercise and nutritional supplementation in primary care settings demonstrated notable improvements in muscle strength, physical function, and body composition, though results varied with study design and adherence.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: High-impact physical activity participation and 12-month risk of joint replacement: a longitudinal mediation analysis of 17 661 patients with knee or hip osteoarthritis
item.description: A longitudinal mediation analysis (n=17,661) found that high-impact physical activity was associated with 36–48% lower odds of total hip replacement (THR) at 12 months, and was not associated with an altered risk of total knee replacement (TKR) in patients with hip or knee osteoarthritis.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Single-bundle versus double-bundle reconstruction in anterior cruciate ligament: a meta-analysis
item.description: A meta-analysis of 41 RCTs (n=3,568) found that DB ACL reconstruction showed statistically higher rates of negative pivot-shift test (short-term OR=0.62, p<0.001; long-term OR=0.37, p=0.007) and higher long-term Lysholm scores (MD=-1.32, p=0.004) compared to SB, but no clinically meaningful superiority for most patients.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: When evidence fails in real life: Rethinking sports injury rehabilitation and prevention.
item.description: This perspective critically examines traditional linear and reductionist models in sports injury prevention and rehabilitation, advocating for a more integrated, complexity-informed framework. It reinterprets evidence-based practice and applies a dynamic biopsychosocial model to better address real-world injury patterns and tailor patient-centered care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of High-Intensity Laser Therapy on Functional Outcomes and Spasticity-Related Pain in Subacute and Chronic Stroke Patients with Plantar Flexor Spasticity: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized sham-controlled trial (n=24) found that high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) combined with conventional rehabilitation for subacute and chronic stroke patients with plantar flexor spasticity significantly reduced spasticity-related pain and showed a covariate-adjusted gait benefit. However, it had no effect on spasticity or muscle thickness, and gait benefits require confirmation in larger trials.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of neuromuscular electrical stimulation combined with blood flow restriction training on lower-leg neuromuscular function in individuals with chronic ankle instability: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=60) found that adding combined neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and blood flow restriction training (BFRT) to an 8-week exercise program for chronic ankle instability patients resulted in higher FAAM-Sports scores than exercise alone and NMES alone, with a broader pattern of favorable changes in secondary outcomes like PL activation and eversion strength.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Machine learning-based identification of a minimal wearable sensor for gait assessment in vestibular schwannoma
item.description: A study used machine learning to identify optimal wearable sensor configurations for gait assessment in vestibular schwannoma, finding that a wrist-worn sensor during eyes-closed gait (FGA8) provided 60-83% accuracy in discriminating patients from controls, suggesting a minimal, clinically deployable solution for objective gait analysis.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: Rotational perturbation training improves muscle coordination during reactive standing balance in trained and untrained conditions in children with spastic cerebral palsy
item.description: A longitudinal intervention study (n=14 children with cerebral palsy) found that 3 weeks of rotational perturbation training improved the ability to maintain standing balance and decreased muscle co-activation and average reactive muscle activity in response to both trained rotational and untrained translational perturbations.
item.author: medRxiv
